chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He who is given three things is not denied three things: He who is given supplication (du'a) is given the answer (ijabah); and he who is given gratitude (shukr) is given increase (ziyadah); and he who is given reliance (tawakkul) is given sufficiency (kifayah).
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Did you recite the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?'
And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him.
And He said: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor].'
And He said: 'Call upon Me, I will answer you.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three spiritual practices that guarantee divine response and increase according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a triad of spiritual causality where supplication, gratitude, and reliance on God yield divine response, increase, and sufficiency, respectively. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the active role of the believer in activating divine mercy through these specific acts of worship. The Imam explicitly links these spiritual states to their Quranic roots, reinforcing the interconnection between human effort and divine grace.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak,

(It has been narrated) from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who gives three (things) would not be denied three (things) – The one who gives the supplication would be Given the answer, and the one gives the thanks would be Given the increase, and the one who gives the reliance would be Given the sufficient’.
Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Did you recite the Book of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[65:3] and whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him?’
And heasws said: ‘[14:7] If you are grateful, I would Increase it more for you.
And Heazwj Said [40:60] And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will Answer you’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father all from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jublah from Muawiyah ibn Wahab from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘To whoever three things are given he is not denied three things. To whoever prayer is given he is given acceptance to his prayer. To whoever thankfulness is given he is given increased favors. To whoever trust is given he is given protection.’
Then He said, ‘Have you read in the book of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy,
“Whoever places his trust in Allah, He provides him sufficient protection.” [14:7]
“If you be thankful We will increase the favor.
Pray to Me, I will accept your prayer.’”” [25:60]
